questions.question: A train can cross a 1200-metre-long bridge completely in 16 seconds. It can cross a 1600-metre-long bridge completely in 20 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of 1st bridge = 1200m and time = 16 seconds

Length of 2nd bridge = 1600m and time = 20 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time 

**Calculation:**

Length of the 1st bridge = 1200m and time = 16 s

Distance = Length of the train + Length of the bridge

Now, Distance = Speed × Time 

⇒ Length of the train + 1200 = Speed × 16

⇔ Length of the train =( 16 speed - 1200)........................................(1)

Now, we have Length of the 2nd bridge = 1600m and time = 20 s

⇒ Distance = Length of the train + Length of the 2nd bridge = Length of the train + 1600

Now, Distance = Speed × 20 

⇒ Length of the train + 1600 = 20 speed ( Put the value of Length of the train from equation(1))

⇒ 16 speed - 1200 + 1600 = 20 Speed

⇒ 400 = 4 × speed ⇔ Speed = 100 m/s 

⇒ Now, to convert m/s into km/h , we have to multiply the number by 18/5

⇒ 100 m/s = 100 × 18/5 = 360 km/h

**Hence, Speed of the train is 360 km/h.**

questions.question: A 280 m long train is running at a speed of 54 km/h. In how much time (in seconds) will it cross a man moving at 12 km/h in the same direction as that of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the train = 280 m

Speed of the train = 54 km/h

Speed of the man = 12 km/h

**Concept used:**

Time = Distance/speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is computed by their difference.

If a train cross a man/pole/tree then it will cover only its own length.

**Calculation:**

Relative speed of the train and the man = (54 - 12) = 42 km/h

Speed in m/sec = 42 × (5/18)

⇒ 35/3 m/sec

Time = 280 ÷ (35/3)

⇒ 280 × (3/35)

⇒ 24 sec

**∴ It will cross the man in 24 seconds.**

questions.question: A 250 metre long train takes 30 seconds to cross a 350 metres long bridge. How much time train will take to cross a 550 metre long bridge?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the Train = 250 m

Length of the first Bridge = 350 m

Length of the second Bridge = 550 m

Time taken to cross = 30 s

**Concept:**

Speed of the Train will be the same while crossing both the two Bridges

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

First we have to calculate the speed of the Train

While crossing the first Bridge,

Total distance = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

⇒ Total distance = (250 + 350) = 600 m

⇒ Speed of the Train = 600/30 = 20 m/s

Now, while crossing the second Bridge,

Total distance = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

⇒ Total distance = (250 + 550) = 800 m

Time = Total distance/Speed of the Train

⇒ Time taken to cross the Bridge of length 550 m = 800/20 = 40 seconds

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. If the length of each train is 540 metres and they cross each other in 54 seconds, then what is the speed of each train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = Sum of train lengths = 540 + 540 = 1080 m.

Relative speed = Total Distance ÷ Time = 1080 ÷ 54 = 20 m/s.

Since both trains are moving in opposite directions at the same speed, relative speed is twice the speed of one train.

Speed of each train = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 m/s.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the first train (L₁) = 540 m

Length of the second train (L₂) = 540 m

Time taken to cross each other (t) = 54 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative speed (when travelling in opposite directions) = v₁ + v₂

Total Distance = L₁ + L₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5b76d77eb7e55161fcbfcb38e596a8b949acdcf1d3281d0bcd36da44a8c390f.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of each train be v m/s.

⇒ Total Distance = 540 + 540 = 1080 m

⇒ Relative Speed = v + v = 2v m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 1080 = 2v × 54

⇒ 1080 = 108v

⇒ v = 1080 ÷ 108

⇒ v = 10 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects travel towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Train Crossing Another Train

The total distance covered by the trains to completely cross each other is always equal to the sum of their lengths, regardless of the direction.

Speed Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the speed by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 73 km/hr and 123 km/hr. The time taken by faster train to cross a man sitting in the slower train is 27 seconds. What will be the length of the faster train?
questions.solution:

Speed of the slower train = 73 km/hr

Speed of the faster train = 123 km/hr

Time taken by the faster train to cross a man in the slower train = 27 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of the faster train - Speed of the slower train

Length of the faster train = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed = 123 km/hr - 73 km/hr

Relative Speed = 50 km/hr

Convert speed from km/hr to m/s:

1 km/hr = (5)/(18) m/s

Relative Speed = 50 × (5)/(18) m/s

Relative Speed = (250)/(18) m/s

Time = 27 seconds

Length of the faster train = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Length of the faster train = (250/18) × 27

⇒ Length of the faster train = 375 meters

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: Two trains running in opposite direction on parallel tracks, at the speed of 48 km/h and 52 km/h, take 27 seconds to cross each other. If the lenght of one train is 350 m then find the length ( in metres) of the other train?

questions.question: Two trains are moving in the same direction at the speed of 34 km/hr and 86 km/hr, their lengths are 300 metres and 480 metres respectively. What will be the time taken by faster train to cross the slower train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the slower train (S1) = 34 km/hr

Speed of the faster train (S2) = 86 km/hr

Length of the slower train (L1) = 300 meters

Length of the faster train (L2) = 480 meters

**Calculations:**

1. Convert Speeds from km/hr to m/s:

⇒ Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5/18)

⇒ Speed of slower train (S1):

⇒ S1 = 34 × (5/18) = 170/18 = 85/9 m/s

⇒ Speed of faster train (S2):

⇒ S2 = 86 × (5/18) = 430/18 = 215/9 m/s

2. Relative Speed:

⇒ Relative Speed = S2 - S1

⇒ = (215/9) - (85/9) = (215 - 85) / 9 = 130/9 m/s

3. Total Length to be Crossed:

⇒ Total Length = L1 + L2 = 300 + 480 = 780 meters

4. Time Taken to Cross:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 780 / (130/9)

⇒ = 780 × (9/130)

⇒ = (780 × 9) / 130

⇒ = 7020 / 130 = 54 seconds

**∴ The time taken by the faster train to cross the slower train is 54 seconds.**

questions.question: Two trains, each 180 m long, are moving towards each other on parallel tracks at speeds of 50 km/hr and 70 km/hr. In how many seconds will they completely cross each other?

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 50 km/hr

Speed of Train 2 (S₂) = 70 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

When two objects are moving towards each other (in opposite directions):

Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

Time Taken = Total Distance Covered ÷ Relative Speed

Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance = 180 + 180 = 360 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 + 70 = 120 km/hr

⇒ To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 120 × (5/18) = 600 / 18 = 100/3 m/s

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 360 ÷ (100/3)

⇒ Time taken = (360 × 3) / 100 = 1080 / 100 = 10.8 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 10.8 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies or trains are moving in the exact same direction, their relative speed is calculated by taking the difference between their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole, tree, or a standing man, the total distance covered is strictly equal to the length of the train itself: Distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ.

Train Crossing a Bridge or Platform

When a train crosses a stationary object that possesses significant length (like a platform, tunnel, or bridge), the total distance covered equals the sum of their respective lengths: Distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ + Lₚₗₐₜfₒᵣₘ.

Speed Conversion Factor

To rapidly convert km/hr to m/s, always multiply the speed value by 5/18. To seamlessly convert m/s back to km/hr, multiply the speed value by 18/5. This derives from 1 km/hr = 1000 meters ÷ 3600 seconds = 5/18 m/s.

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses a stationary object of negligible length (like an electric pole or a standing man), the distance traveled is equal to the length of the train itself. When crossing another train or a platform, the distance traveled is the sum of their lengths: L₁ + L₂.
